adjudication_anchor: Introduction/contributions and §§5–6; generation-volume and selected-paper reporting
adjudication_rationale: The paper describes the capacity to generate hundreds of papers and provides selected and aggregate results, but does not reconcile every initiated idea/run with failed, stopped, retried and no-paper states. The initial research-unit denominator is therefore unrecoverable.

adjudication_anchor: §4.1 and Fig. 3 (44-iteration discovery); Appendix J.1, Tables 22–23 (20-case ablation)
adjudication_rationale: The two components of the stated target are explicitly finite: the discovery ledger contains 44 iterations, and the verifier ablation contains 16 planted failures plus four clean controls. Both successes and failure/control states are enumerated.

adjudication_anchor: §3 pipelines; §4 and appendix generation, clustering and matching tables
adjudication_rationale: Per-model generation volumes are reported, but the union-of-runs estimand is formed after clustering, deduplication and idea–innovation pair construction. The paper does not provide one fully reconciled count from all initiated raw ideas through those transformations.

adjudication_anchor: §6.1 process statistics; Appendix protocol at lines 1365–1431
adjudication_rationale: The protocol states 44 total experiments and records terminal and nonterminal states, including falsified, cratered, skipped and still-running work. Exclusion from three-seed evaluation is a recorded state rather than loss from the initial denominator.

adjudication_anchor: §3 benchmark construction; Tables 2–3 and complete appendix framework–theme score tables
adjudication_rationale: The target unit is a framework–theme final output. Eleven frameworks crossed with five themes yields exactly 55 units, all represented in the benchmark tables; undisclosed internal reasoning attempts are not additional units for this target.

adjudication_anchor: Pipeline §2 and selected-paper analyses in §§5–6
adjudication_rationale: Review and detailed analysis operate on papers that completed the pipeline or were selected for presentation. The paper supplies neither a common endpoint for every initiated research unit nor a prespecified probability sample with known inclusion.

adjudication_anchor: §2.3–2.6, especially §2.4 Conducting Experiments and §2.5 Manuscripts; Table 1
adjudication_rationale: All 12 planned ideas receive execution accounting, but manuscript-level scientific assessment is necessarily restricted to the seven successfully executed experiments. The design therefore covers the full funnel but does not apply one manuscript-validity procedure to every initiated idea.

adjudication_anchor: §4 evaluation, lines 396–418 and 518–540; Appendix C.7 Table 14
adjudication_rationale: Each of 64 hypotheses is run ten times against the same ground truth. Crucially, the reported end-to-end analysis counts execution failures as incorrect, providing an all-run endpoint rather than conditioning solely on valid outputs.

adjudication_anchor: §1 funnel, lines 129–150; automated and human review protocol in §§2–3
adjudication_rationale: The 48-target funnel remains visible, and automated review covers the valid-length manuscripts, but structured human scientific-validity review is confined to ten automated accepts. Coverage is substantial but outcome-conditioned.

adjudication_anchor: Abstract and §4 selection/transfer analysis
adjudication_rationale: The confirmatory next-model transfer endpoint is applied only to configurations selected for having produced a false positive on the prior model. This is an outcome-conditioned subset, not all initial cells or a prespecified probability sample.

adjudication_anchor: §4 human review; Appendix Human review protocol, lines 610–637
adjudication_rationale: Human confirmation is limited to 519 idea–future-innovation pairs shortlisted by an LLM novelty/matching stage. The unreviewed generated pairs are neither assigned the same endpoint nor sampled probabilistically.

adjudication_anchor: §3.3 evaluation protocol; Tables 2–3 and appendix score tables
adjudication_rationale: All 55 framework–theme outputs are evaluated with the same stage-specific ACS rubrics and fixed aggregation procedure. Variation by stage is prespecified within a common protocol, not selective validation.

adjudication_anchor: Abstract and §1, lines 30–33 and 68–100; workshop-review description
adjudication_rationale: The three selected manuscripts were submitted to a real ICLR workshop and assessed by its peer-review process, which is institutionally external to the generating pipeline and its internal selector.

adjudication_anchor: §4.2 Human Expert Evaluation; §4.3 and Fig. 4
adjudication_rationale: A human program committee provides review and the authors analyze failed implementations, but expert validation covers selected papers/subsets while much of the 4879-to-1108-to-21 filtering and validation remains internal. Independence is therefore only partial for the target funnel.

adjudication_anchor: Table 1 and §3 evaluation, PDF pp. 1–4
adjudication_rationale: All 20 problem-agent attempts are judged by human mathematical experts procedurally separated from proof generation, including external specialists. Team selection of experts and occasional disagreement affect uncertainty but do not negate procedural independence.

adjudication_anchor: §1 contributions, lines 94–111; §3 ground-truth construction, lines 396–400; Appendix ground-truth notes
adjudication_rationale: Reference statistics and verdicts are established from the datasets and validated by domain experts before comparison with tested agent outputs. This prespecified reference process is separated from generation and selection.

adjudication_anchor: §4 benchmark/scoring and annotation method, PDF lines 229–240 and 742–763
adjudication_rationale: Fixed task scorers are separated from evaluated agent configurations and two annotators examine reasoning traces, but the environment and proxy labels are author-built and full-corpus independent human coding is absent. The mixed procedure supports partial independence.

adjudication_anchor: §1 discussion of reviewer feedback, lines 80–100; workshop reviews
adjudication_rationale: External workshop reviews address technical soundness and research quality of the three manuscripts, which is validity-relevant, but review scores and acceptance-worthiness do not reproduce or independently establish the full experimental claims.

Execution and SOTA comparisons test empirical soundness, and expert review examines selected papers, but the 21 'scientific innovations' combine internal progress filters, benchmark gains and selected review rather than one direct all-unit scientific-validity endpoint.

adjudication_anchor: §2.3 ECO; §4 accuracy/completion evaluation; Tables 3–5
adjudication_rationale: The endpoint compares evidence labels and final verdicts for clinical hypotheses against expert-validated dataset-derived ground truth, explicitly distinguishing supported, refuted, underpowered and invalid states. This directly measures scientific hypothesis-testing correctness.

adjudication_anchor: Held-out transfer definition at lines 223–237; Tables 2–4
adjudication_rationale: The target claim is that each adaptively selected intervention improves prediction on unseen material data. A frozen, once-only hidden outer evaluation directly tests that narrow empirical generalization claim, so the endpoint is scientific validity rather than mere in-loop score.
